title: Light breeze gave no clear change in warmth slopes of frog calling richness in four US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether wind changed the link between survey-night temperature and the number of four fixed frog species heard. We used 11,013 NAAMP runs on 685 routes in the Northeast and Midwest, split into 2001-2007 and 2008-2015. Models controlled route-year, route-observer, season and curved temperature terms. The change in the 5 C warmth slope at a light breeze versus calm ranged from -0.068 to +0.032 mean detected species per stop. All four 98.75 percent route-cluster intervals included zero. Two-way route and year intervals and six model or sample checks did not change this result. The later Northeast estimate was negative, but its sign did not repeat in the other samples. Selected survey nights, reported wind classes, missing rain reports and mixed calling and hearing effects limit inference. This is a test of an observation index, not true richness, population change, climate trends or air pollution. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and a retrieval recipe are included.
